why: The student gives the correct answer (String) and backs it with one correct rule, that String is a class. They identify which types are primitive, but they don't relate the types to any other construct or to the code, so this is L1.

concepts.why: Correctly names int, double, boolean and char as primitive types, but says nothing about how they behave in the code.
Correctly says String is a non-primitive class type; this is one correct fact that isn't applied to anything.

concepts.quote: String; it is a class. The other four are primitive.
concepts.why: Splits the types into primitive and class, but doesn't mention that a variable holds either a value or a reference.
Says nothing about data types as sets of values and operations.
